brief: A recipe manager as a transformation timeline — ingredients flow through steps and combine into the dish

dominant_strengths: Clear stage taxonomy with color-coded category pills (PREP/SEAR/BRAISE/FINISH) gives the timeline a readable rhythm and hierarchy
Final dish card with warm amber glow creates a satisfying narrative endpoint, reinforcing the transformation metaphor
Numbered step badges and arrow connectors make the sequential flow legible at a glance
dominant_weaknesses: Ingredient column on the left is clipped off-canvas, breaking the core 'ingredients flow into steps' premise the brief promises
Vast empty upper canvas wastes vertical space; timeline floats low and feels ungrounded with no header-to-content connection
No visual flow lines from individual ingredients to the steps they enter — the 'transformation' is implied, not shown
fix_priorities: Repair layout so ingredients panel is fully visible and connected with curved flow lines into relevant step cards
Rebalance vertical composition — pull timeline up or add contextual content (timing axis, temperature) to fill dead space
Differentiate the four step pills more (BRAISE red is distinct, but PREP/FINISH both lean green/purple ambiguously)
Add micro-typographic hierarchy inside step cards — tagline italics or smaller meta text to separate intent from actions
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept (cooking-as-transformation) outpaces visceral polish and behavioral completeness, since the ingredient-to-step linkage is missing.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fulfills the brief — the timeline and convergence to the dish are present, but ingredients don't visibly 'flow' into steps, weakening the central transformation metaphor.
